62 of 97 Survived the Hindenburg. Where.caption:
62 of 97 Survived the Hindenburg. Where You Stood Decided Who Lived.

Ninety-seven people were on the Hindenburg when it burned. Sixty-two survived. The difference was where they happened to be standing.

She Threw Her Sons Out of the Hindenburg Window. Then She Jumped.

When the Hindenburg sank toward the ground, Matilde Doehner threw her two young sons out of the dining-room window, then jumped after them. All three lived.

On Mai Khao beach in Phuket, 10-year-old Tilly Smith recognised the warning signs from a geography lesson two weeks earlier. Her parents warned the beach and the hotel staff. No one on that beach was killed.

Scientists in Hawaii Knew About the 2004.caption:
Scientists in Hawaii Knew About the 2004 Earthquake in Minutes. Why Couldn't They Warn Anyone?

About eight minutes after the earthquake off Sumatra, an alarm went off at the Pacific Tsunami Warning Center. But in 2004 the Indian Ocean had no tsunami warning system and no deep-ocean sensors, and the countries in the wave's path weren't on the Pacific list.

Would You Know a Tsunami Was Coming?.caption:
Would You Know a Tsunami Was Coming?

Out at sea, a tsunami can be less than a metre high and still move as fast as a jet. In 2004, two warning signs saved lives: the ground shaking hard, and the sea pulling back. Swipe through, then tell us: did anyone ever teach you these signs?

Why Did a Whole Village Climb Onto a Tra.caption:
Why Did a Whole Village Climb Onto a Train in 2004?

The first wave stopped the Queen of the Sea near Peraliya, Sri Lanka, and people from the village climbed onto the carriages to get above the water. Then bigger waves came. Guinness World Records lists it as the worst train disaster on record.
